claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The HfNbTaTiZr material may contain defects or impurities such as oxygen.
The proposed intervention is ab initio molecular dynamics with explicit defect and impurity models.
Molecular-dynamics modeling can explicitly connect atomistic lattice structure and defects to simulated behavior.
Defects and impurities affect lattice thermal conductivity through phonon scattering.
Explicitly modeling defects and impurities will predict a 15% increase in the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr at 300 K relative to a perfect, defect-free bulk-crystal model.
The prediction is intended to apply from 300 to 1200 K.
A perfect, defect-free bulk-crystal model provides the baseline for the predicted improvement.
The magnitude of the predicted conductivity increase may depend on the identities and concentrations of defects and impurities.
The model should be tested against experimental lattice thermal conductivity at 300 K while measuring defect and impurity concentrations.
A discrepancy greater than 10% between modeled and experimental lattice thermal conductivity would falsify the hypothesis.
